AI agents are now the main attacker behind most of 2026’s breaches. Almost none of it needed a new trick: 79% still came down to a stolen key, token or credential.

The finding comes from The State of the NHI & AI Agent Breach Report 2026, released this week by our friends at NHI Mgmt Group. They analysed 200+ real breaches from 2017 to October 2026, across more than 1,000 public sources. A few of the numbers that stood out to us:

✔️ 33 of the 53 breaches they tracked in 2026 involved AI agents, LLM platforms or AI attack routes.
✔️ 44% of all breaches began with a leaked, stolen or weak credential.
✔️ 56% involved more than one kind of non-human identity.
✔️ Supply chain is now the number one known way in, where one stolen token can reach every downstream user.

One leaked key rarely stays one key. A single credential reaches the next secret, then cloud roles, then the data, often without a single alert. And we know these credentials will most likely leak. What decides the damage is what that credential, or a hijacked agent, can reach once it is inside.

NHI Mgmt Group are very clear about the fact that the inventory, scope and short credential lifetimes matter more than any single control.

Controlling the scope and lifetime of access is the work PlainID does. We enforce runtime authorization and Zero Standing Privileges across human, non-human and AI agent identities, so a compromised key reaches only what policy allows at that moment, not everything it inherited.

You can access the full report here 👉 https://hubs.ly/Q04BT7NL0 | PlainID
